scope: Path F evaluation for Row D-3-c (audience_did at apply_atrium_merge): writes self-attest via grant_chain reference
summary: Path F is structurally feasible at v1-beta and aligns elegantly with the project's code-as-graph + plugins-as-subgraphs philosophy: the LOCAL write path already names a `capability_grant_cid: Option<Cid>` field on `PendingOp::PutNode` + `ChangeEvent` + `AttributionFrame` (engine_caps L630 already threads a chain anchor via `WriteAdmissionFrame::with_chain`). The structural gap Path F closes is at the SYNC WIRE: `apply_atrium_merge` hard-codes `capability_grant_cid: Cid::from_blake3_digest([0u8; 32])` at engine.rs:1634 because the Loro `StampedValue` wire shape (crdt.rs:174) carries only `value + hlc` — the writer-side grant_cid is information-lost crossing the CRDT boundary. Recommended sub-flavor F-1 (the elegant permanent shape): grant_cid as a SIBLING field on a new versioned `StampedValueV2 { value, hlc, grant_cid: Option<Cid> }` wire payload, NOT as a property on the user Node (option (i) cascades through user-CID stability and is the wrong place). Cap-policy hook signature extends `CapWriteContext { ..., authorizing_grant_cid: Option<Cid> }` (sibling to existing `actor_cid` + `audience_did`); audience-aware impls derive audience from grant via in-graph `system:CapabilityGrant` lookup at recheck time (already routinely done by `EngineCapsHandle::revoke_capability_by_grant_cid` at engine_caps.rs:278+). LOC: ~1100-1500 across 6 surfaces; cross-cuts heavily with G-CORE-PQ-WIRE (binding_sig shape change in same wave-window). Refinement: the wire-bump MUST land in the same wave as G-CORE-PQ-WIRE — both are pre-v1-beta-tag wire-format-window mutations on identity-bearing surfaces; merging them avoids two consecutive wire breaks for downstream peers.

findings.title: Q1: Current grant-identification mechanism at per-row recheck — scope-walking, NOT grant_cid-threaded
findings.summary: `GrantBackedPolicy::check_write` at grant_backed.rs:484 calls `self.grants.has_unrevoked_grant_matching(scope, actor_cid)` — pure (scope, optional actor) lookup; no grant_cid is presented by the caller. `UcanGroundedPolicy::check_write` at ucan_grounded.rs:418 has a fast-path delegating to GrantBackedPolicy (same shape) then a slow-path that derives `audience` from `ctx.actor_hint`'s DID and walks the typed-cap proof chain. Neither consumes a grant_cid. This is option (a)+(b) hybrid from the brief: principal's grant store walked by scope, optionally filtered by actor_cid.

findings.implication: Path F's structural delta = adding `authorizing_grant_cid: Option<Cid>` to CapWriteContext (sibling to existing `audience_did` + `actor_cid`); cap-policy impls that opt-in to grant_cid-driven dispatch consult the in-graph `system:CapabilityGrant` Node directly (`engine.read_node` style) rather than walking the principal's grant store. Existing scope-based policies remain backward-compat (ignore the new field).

findings.title: Q2: grant_cid SHOULD live in the SYNC WIRE ENVELOPE (option ii), NOT in user Node properties (option i)
findings.summary: Option (i) — grant_cid as a property like `system:authorization_grant_cid` on the user Node — would mutate the user Node's CID per crates/benten-core/src/lib.rs:189-202 (`Node` CID = hash(labels + properties), `anchor_id` excluded via `#[serde(skip)]`). This forces every plugin/user write to carry a different CID pre/post Path F — a SUBSTANTIAL canonical-bytes break that ripples through every test fixture, every #843 golden-CID test, every cross-peer convergence assertion. Option (ii) — grant_cid in the sync-merge envelope alongside `StampedValue` — keeps user CIDs stable and confines the wire change to a single versioned struct: `StampedValueV2 { value, hlc, grant_cid: Option<Cid> }`. Option (iii) — graph edge from row to grant Node — works at the local-graph layer but doesn't survive the Loro CRDT round-trip without ALSO appearing on the wire (the edge would need to be ship-on-the-merge-bytes). Option (ii) is the structurally correct answer: writes are self-attesting at the WIRE LAYER (the sync envelope), not at the content-addressed user-data layer. The local-graph projection (option iii edge from row to grant) is the post-merge consequence of the wire-attestation, applied by `apply_atrium_merge` after the row lands.

The merge-Version-Node CID change IS in scope per the v1-beta wire-format-freeze window (CLAUDE.md baked-in #15 / G-CORE-9 freeze contract).

findings.title: Q4: Forward-compat to multi-device + Garden-Grove untrusted-host + Kith selective-disclosure
findings.summary: Multi-device (Phase-3 LIVE): writer = Alice; relay-peer = Alice's-phone. Path F: Alice's-laptop signs the write under grant_cid X (Alice's self-grant); Alice's-phone relays the merge bytes carrying grant_cid X. Receiving peer Bob looks up grant X in HIS local copy of the graph (UCAN chain delivered separately via UCAN-blobs protocol per ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:109 — already exists). Path F works HERE. Garden-Grove (Phase-7+) untrusted-host: peer X holds Alice's ciphertext for Alice. X relays Alice's writes — wire grant_cid is Alice's grant; X has NO grant of his own to substitute. Path F holds; X cannot forge a grant_cid that Alice's-recipient-peer can validate (binding_sig of AuthorizationGrant defends per authorization_grant.rs:653 `verify_binding`). Kith selective-disclosure (Phase-7+): identity-view-projection — the projection is a READ pattern (the writer still signed under their full grant; the projector restricts the read). Path F at the WRITE side is orthogonal to selective-read; the existing IVM read-gate composes. CRITICAL CAVEAT: at relay, the grant ITSELF must be discoverable. Today UcanBlobsRequest at ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:114 carries the full grant on the wire for blob fetches. For CRDT row merges, the grant_cid in the wire envelope is a CID REFERENCE — the receiving peer needs to actually have/fetch the grant Node bytes to verify. RECOMMENDED REFINEMENT: pair Path F with a grant-CID-resolution port (`GrantResolver` trait at benten-caps) — `fn resolve_grant(cid: &Cid) -> Result<AuthorizationGrant>`. Default impl reads from local backend; production impl can fetch via UCAN-blobs protocol if missing locally. This is exactly the post-Phase-3 grant-fetch infrastructure that should exist at v1-beta.

findings.title: Q6: Cross-cuts with in-flight waves — G-CORE-PQ-WIRE is the natural wave-pair
findings.summary: (a) G-CORE-PQ-WIRE (Row D-26) is the dedicated multi-wave initiative changing identity-bearing-surface signature shape at v1-beta — including `AuthorizationGrant::binding_sig` at authorization_grant.rs:247 (already named at Row D-15e re-homed per V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md:1102-1104). Path F changes the SYNC WIRE in the same v1-beta-wire-format-freeze window. RECOMMENDATION: bundle Path F into the G-CORE-PQ-WIRE wave (or sequence Path F immediately AFTER G-CORE-PQ-WIRE within the same window) — both wave-form a single wire-bump for downstream peers rather than two consecutive breaks. (b) Compromise #11 IVM views read-gate: per-row recheck IS the IVM read-gate input surface; Path F enriches what info is available at IVM eval time (writer's grant_cid). The IVM read-gate's `IvmViewReadGate::admits(row_cid)` signature stays unchanged (the gate consults the actor's cap set; grant_cid enriches the WRITER side, not the READER side). NO IVM cascade. (c) CLAUDE.md baked-in #5 (canonical bytes contract): MerketVersion Node CID changes (from zero-stuffed AttributionFrame to substantively-populated); already absorbed by serde-skip-on-default. User Node CIDs UNCHANGED. (d) Inv-13 immutability (system-zone prefix reject at engine.rs:1327-1338): unaffected — the new grant_cid lives in the wire envelope, not as a property key. (e) Inv-14 device-grain attribution: composes cleanly; AttributionFrame already extends device_did + grant_cid sibling-style.

findings.title: Q7: Alternative Path F-2 — sibling `system:WriteAuthorization` Node with edge to row and edge to grant
findings.summary: Alternative F-2: don't add grant_cid to wire envelope; instead the OUTBOUND sync also ships a sibling `system:WriteAuthorization` Node carrying { row_cid, grant_cid, writer_did } + an edge `AUTHORIZED_BY` from row to grant. Pros: keeps StampedValue wire shape unchanged; uses existing edge/Node machinery; consistent with code-as-graph philosophy. Cons: (a) requires sync to ship multiple Nodes per row (~3x wire bloat for high-write-volume scenarios), (b) atomic-merge semantics — what if the WriteAuthorization Node lands but the row doesn't, or vice versa? Requires synchronized landing discipline at apply_atrium_merge, (c) sync_subgraph/share boundary needs to compute + ship the WriteAuthorization Nodes per row (substantive refactor at the outbound side). RECOMMENDATION: Path F-2 is WORSE than F-1 — F-1's wire-envelope `grant_cid` is the smallest delta achieving the same semantic (writers self-attest at the wire layer). F-1 wins on (a) wire compactness, (b) atomic-merge (one row carries its own attestation), (c) outbound simplicity (just plumb grant_cid through set_property). F-2 is preserved as a fallback if v1-beta wire-format-freeze closes BEFORE Path F can land — then attestation moves to a per-row Node + edge addition, which is wire-format-COMPATIBLE (just additional Nodes).
findings.implication: F-1 (wire-envelope sibling field) is the recommended PRIMARY implementation; F-2 (sibling Node + edge) is the post-v1-beta fallback if the wire window closes.
